response.sql: SELECT s.insurstat AS insurstat, COUNT(DISTINCT c.zoneref) AS site_count, COUNT(DISTINCT c.zoneref) * 1.0 / SUM(COUNT(DISTINCT c.zoneref)) OVER () AS share FROM scanconservation c JOIN sites s ON s.zoneregistry = c.zoneref GROUP BY s.insurstat

assumptions.assumption: "Count the conserved sites" means distinct sites that have at least one conservation record, not the number of conservation records. A site has one insurance status, so the counts add up to the total number of distinct conserved sites.
A missing status means a NULL insurstat. NULLs form their own group, shown as NULL. Empty strings are not treated as missing.
The share is the status count divided by the sum of all status counts, as an unrounded decimal fraction between 0 and 1. It is not a percentage.

alternatives.interpretation: Count conservation records per insurance status instead of distinct sites, so a site with several conservation records is counted several times.
alternatives.sql: SELECT s.insurstat AS insurstat, COUNT(*) AS record_count, COUNT(*) * 1.0 / SUM(COUNT(*)) OVER () AS share FROM scanconservation c JOIN sites s ON s.zoneregistry = c.zoneref GROUP BY s.insurstat
